title: Strong existence for SDEs with singular drifts driven by fractional Brownian motion
summary: Let $B^H$ be a $d$-dimensional fractional Brownian motion with Hurst parameter $H\in(0,1/2)$. We prove the existence of a strong solution to $$d X_t=b(t,X_t)d t+d B_t^H, X_0=x_0\in R^d,$$when $b\in L^q([0,T];L^p(\mathbb R^d;\mathbb R^d)),2\le p,q<\infty$ and the subcritical Ladyzhenskaya--Prodi--Serrin condition $\frac1q+\frac{Hd}{p}<1-H$ is satisfied. Thus, within the finite-exponent range $p,q\ge2$, the strong-existence result covers the full subcritical region, including the regime $p<2Hd$, where a uniform strong Novikov condition may fail. The proof is based on a compactness criterion…
